text:
The evidence can't tell us whether fire caused the loss. It confirms that tree cover was lost, but it doesn't identify the cause.

What it shows: Hansen/UMD mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021 within the asset (2.23% of its area). A later year was observed and the JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on 98% of the event area, so the loss is corroborated. Most of it (68.1 ha) falls in planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), and 13.2 ha is outside mapped forest.

What it doesn't show: Hansen loss captures any stand replacement, such as harvest, fire, storm or clearing. The data doesn't distinguish among them, so it can't confirm or rule out fire. Given the planted-pine context, routine harvest is a plausible alternative, but that's not established either.

To test for fire, you'd need burned-area products or fire-alert data (e.g., MODIS/VIIRS, Sentinel-2 burn scars), local fire records, or harvest permits for 2021.
